Looking at this question, I need to consider the mandarin (Citrus reticulata) genome characteristics.

The mandarin genome is approximately 472 Mb in size, with transposable elements (TEs) making up roughly 27-30% of the genome (~130 Mb of TE sequences). 

Given that individual transposable elements typically range from a few hundred base pairs to several kilobases in length (averaging around 10 kb), the total number of TE insertions in ~130 Mb of TE-rich genomic sequence would be in the range of approximately 12,000-13,000 sites.

Among the options, 12,300 is the only number that aligns with the expected scale of TE insertion loci in a genome of this size and TE content.

[ANSWER]J[/ANSWER]
